title: Replace fixed-duration Future.delayed sleeps with deterministic sync in gamification reactive-stream tests
why: These 3 files (10 occurrences total) use hard-coded 20/50/150ms real-time sleeps as the only synchronization before asserting a Drift Stream has propagated a new emission, with no retry/poll and no use of pumpEventQueue() (confirmed 0 usages repo-wide). On a loaded CI runner a slower-than-budgeted FFI round-trip would fail the assertion with no code regression involved — exactly the kind of flake that erodes trust in the 'staleness regression' suite meant to guard DG-RDMP-01/02 and DG-PND-05.
recommendation: Replace `Future.delayed(fixedDuration)` with `pumpEventQueue()` or a small poll-until-condition helper bounded by a generous timeout, so the wait tracks actual event-loop drain rather than a guessed duration.
acceptance_criteria: No test in these 3 files gates its only assertion on a bare Future.delayed(fixed duration); a poll/pumpEventQueue-based helper is used instead.
